title: Holistic Acceptance Matrix for Model Promotion
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: This page defines a single, reproducible acceptance matrix and workflow used by Redwood Inference to decide whether a candidate model (or model variant) may be promoted to staging and production. The matrix covers automated evals, human checks, performance/latency budgets, quantization acceptance, and regression-triage triggers. It is intended to reduce ambiguity in promotions and standardize cross-team expectations.
purpose: Provide a deterministic set of checks, metrics, and decision rules for onboarding new model versions across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The matrix balances quality, cost, and operational safety and ties results to rollout constraints and rollback criteria.
scope: Applies to all model artifacts that will be served through Redwood API, Dedicated pools, or Private deployments. Includes open-source base models and any internal fine-tuned variants. Excludes short-lived experimental snapshots that are explicitly labeled "experimental" and not intended for promotion.
acceptance_matrix_overview: The acceptance matrix groups checks into five axes: 1) Functional quality (task-specific metrics & human eval), 2) Safety and policy (toxicity, PII leakage, hallucination), 3) Performance (latency, memory, KV-cache behavior), 4) Cost/efficiency (tokens-per-second, batch throughput, quantized accuracy delta), and 5) Reliability/regression stability (rolling-average error, tail latency, CI integration). A candidate must pass all mandatory gates and must not have non-triaged showstopper regressions.
metrics_and_thresholds:
Key automated metrics and baseline thresholds (adapt per workload):

- Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) on canonical prompts: baseline >= 0.88 (relative to current prod mean).
- Human-eval pass rate (task-specific) on holdout prompt set: >= 85% agreed pass.
- Hallucination / factuality failure rate: <= 3% on factual-check set.
- Toxicity (model score, internal classifier): <= 1% of responses flagged high-risk; must pass targeted adversarial toxicity subset.
- Response diversity: Distinct-1 >= 0.12 and Distinct-2 >= 0.06 on generative tasks where diversity matters.
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency for standard short prompts (<= 128 tokens) must not exceed prod baseline by more than +20% and absolute p95 target <= 150ms for dedicated-tier targets.
- Memory / KV cache footprint: increase <= 10% vs baseline for same sequence lengths.
- Quantization accuracy delta (when proposing quantized variant): metric degradation <= 2% absolute on critical task metrics and latency improvement >= 15% vs float baseline.
- CI regression windows: rolling 7-day error-rate delta <= +2 percentage points vs prod.

Notes: teams can tighten per-customer SLAs (e.g., enterprise-tier latency targets) by adding custom checks into the promotion pipeline.
evaluation_workflow:
1) Pre-flight: generate model card, artifact digest, reproducible evaluation recipe (seeded), and identify canonical prompt groups (functional, adversarial, safety, long-context).
2) Automated batch evals: run eval harness with production-like serving simulator; capture metrics above and produce a structured report.
3) Quantization bench (if applicable): run quantize profile with per-workload verifier and adversarial prompts; produce numeric delta table.
4) Human validation: sample 200 responses across prompt groups; pairwise annotation by two raters and an adjudicator for disagreements.
5) Security & privacy scan: automated PII detectors + manual review for data exposure risks.
6) Stakeholder review: engineering + product + security sign-off meeting if any gate is close to threshold.
7) Staging rollout: deploy to staging routing slice and run canary traffic for 72 hours with synthetic workload injection and real traffic shadowing.
8) Promotion: scheduled canary to production following stepwise ramp (see rollout_policy).

CLI snippets for reproducible evals: 
redwood-eval run --model candidate:v{hash} --recipe eval-recipes/canonical-prompts.yaml --out report.json
redwood-quant-bench --model candidate:v{hash} --profile low-bit --out quant_report.json
onboarding_checklist:
Mandatory items (all must be completed and attached to the promotion ticket):

1. Model card: architecture, training data summary, license, intended use, known limitations.
2. Artifact checksum and provenance (git commit, storage URI).
3. Automated eval report (report.json) with raw metrics + thresholds table.
4. Human validation summary with annotator agreement stats.
5. Quantization report (if proposing quantized variant).
6. Security & PII scan results.
7. Load/perf bench: throughput and latency curves for expected shard sizes.
8. Rollout plan with canary percentages, monitoring dashboards, and rollback criteria.
9. Owner and on-call rotation for the first 72 hours post-promotion.
10. Link to smoke-test scripts and automated post-deploy checks.

Optional but recommended: glossary of prompts used and a one-page summary for non-engineering reviewers.
roles_and_ownership:
- Model Owner: responsible for pre-flight artifacts, addressing triage items, and owning the promotion ticket.
- Eval Owner: runs the eval harness and is responsible for reproducibility and result integrity.
- Quantization Owner: runs quant profiles and verifies accuracy/throughput tradeoffs.
- Security Reviewer: performs PII and policy checks.
- Release Manager: schedules staging and production rollout and verifies that monitoring is in place.
- Oncall/Support: assigned for 72 hours post-promotion for immediate rollback or mitigation.

Primary escalation path: Model Owner -> Eval Owner -> Release Manager -> Head of Platform if cross-cutting issues are unresolved in 4 hours.
rollout_and_monitoring:
Stepwise rollout policy (default):

- Canary 1: 1% traffic for 2 hours; automated smoke checks (error-rate, p50/p95 latency, basic quality probes).
- Canary 2: 5% traffic for 6 hours; expanded quality probes and adversarial prompt injection.
- Canary 3: 25% for 24 hours; monitor rolling metrics and customer-specific tests.
- Full: 100% after 24–72 hours of stable canary windows.

Automated monitors to enable before rollout: latency p95, error rate, model quality regression probe (synthetic prompts), safety classifier alerts, token-cost deltas, and end-to-end customer flows.

Rollback triggers (any of these cause immediate rollback to previous stable variant):
- sustained error-rate increase > 3 percentage points for 30 minutes,
- latency p95 increase > 30% for 30 minutes,
- human-eval quality probe drop > 2 absolute points,
- safety classifier high-risk alert rate spikes > 2x baseline, or
- severe production incidents reported by customers.
failure_modes_and_triage:
Common failure modes and suggested triage actions: 

- Quality regression on a narrow prompt cluster: run per-prompt delta analysis, revert fine-tuning changes for that cluster, and add targeted augmentations.
- Increased hallucination on long-context tasks: check KV-cache alignment, reproduce in serving simulator with extended seq lengths, and compare attention activations to baseline.
- Latency regressions under batching: validate kernel selection and continuous-batching settings; run microbenchmarks with identical request distributions.
- Quantization-induced semantic drift: compare attention similarity, run per-layer sensitivity, and consider mixed-precision fallback for critical layers.
- Safety classifier false negatives: expand adversarial safety prompt set, re-evaluate classifier threshold, and escalate to Security Reviewer for annotation refresh.

Triage process: create a regression ticket, tag with affected metric and prompt IDs, assign to Model Owner and Eval Owner, run targeted replayed evaluations, and decide patch vs rollback within 24 hours for production incidents.

appendix_examples_and_tables:
Example acceptance checklist table (CSV-style):

item, gate, metric, threshold, status
model-card, mandatory, present, yes, PASS
automated-sim-eval, mandatory, semantic-sim >= 0.88, 0.892, PASS
human-eval, mandatory, pass-rate >= 0.85, 0.86, PASS
quantized-delta, conditional, accuracy-delta <= 0.02, 0.015, PASS
latency-p95, mandatory, <= baseline*1.2, baseline*1.05, PASS
safety-toxic, mandatory, flagged <= 0.01, 0.008, PASS

Use this table as a quick copy-paste into promotion tickets to show gating results at a glance.
next_steps_and_improvements: We will iterate on thresholds and probe sets quarterly. Action items: expand long-context factual checks, standardize diversity metrics for creative tasks, and integrate cost-aware routing tests into the gating system. Please file feedback against this page or open a ticket labeled 'model-onboarding-matrix-feedback'.
